title: Completed stalk comparisons and source reparametrization
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$. Let $Z\xrightarrow{h}Y\xrightarrow{f}X$ be morphisms of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the derived-complete integral constructible categories [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], their raw rationalizations [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and the completed pullbacks of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Specify their composition comparisons by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ or $E$, any one of these schemes $T$, a geometric point $v:s\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and $M\in D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$, put $J_v(M)=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}(Lv^*M)$, with [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. In the comparison for $f$ below take $v:s\to Y$ and $M\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$; in the reparametrization comparison take $M$ on the target of $v$.

There are natural $\Lambda$-linear comparison isomorphisms
$$c_{f,v,M}:J_v(Lf^*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{fv}(M),\qquad r_{v,\alpha,M}:J_v(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{v\delta}(M),\quad\delta=\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha),\quad\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(k).$$
Here $c$ uses the specified pullback-composition comparison, and $r$ is normalized by the finite-level germ rule $[U,u,a]\mapsto[U,u\delta,a]$ in [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. Their integral constructions realize these comparisons as maps of the simultaneous strict reduction diagrams, using the comparisons of [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence]; their rational constructions are their images under rationalization. In particular, the asserted equalities are equalities of those specified maps, not merely equality of their individual reductions.

For $w:s\to Z$, write $\chi_{h,f}:L(fh)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lf^*$. Then
$$c_{fh,w,M}=c_{f,hw,M}\circ c_{h,w,Lf^*M}\circ J_w(\chi_{h,f,M}),\qquad c_{\mathrm{id},v,M}=1,$$
$$r_{fv,\alpha,M}\circ c_{f,v,M}=c_{f,v\delta,M}\circ r_{v,\alpha,Lf^*M}.$$
If $\epsilon=\operatorname{Spec}(\beta)$, then $r_{v\delta,\beta,M}\circ r_{v,\alpha,M}=r_{v,\beta\circ\alpha,M}$, and $r_{v,1,M}=1$; equivalently the composite reparametrizes by $\delta\circ\epsilon$. All these comparisons are natural in arbitrary morphisms of the specified integral or rational categories.

For $N\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ and any such $\delta$, let $j_{\delta,N}:\operatorname{Fib}_sN\to\operatorname{Fib}_sL\delta^*N$ be restriction of sections along $\delta$, followed by inverse-image colimit insertion and the inverse-image/pullback comparison of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] (and rationalization for $E$). Under the identity-point identification $J_{\mathrm{id}}(N)=\operatorname{Fib}_sN$, one has
$$c_{\delta,\mathrm{id},N}\circ j_{\delta,N}=r_{\mathrm{id},\alpha,N}.$$
This last equation is compatible with any finite succession of source automorphisms and with the comparisons for $v:s\to X$. No Weil structure, periodic point, or endomorphism of $M$ is assumed.

Agent refinement to completed integral/rational stalks using the specified strict-system realization; blueprint thm-trf-l-function-euler-product.proof.md, Step 1, Local powers, input (b).

proof.text: Write $R=\mathcal O_E$. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to M$ and its simultaneous quotient tower $P_n=P\otimes_{\widehat R_T}(A_n)_T$, with actual quotient transitions, by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. The reductions have cohomology in one interval $[a,b]$ by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. To apply the bounded-complex finite stalk theorem, use the functorial zigzag $P_\bullet\leftarrow\tau_{\le b}P_\bullet\to\tau_{\ge a}\tau_{\le b}P_\bullet=:B_\bullet$. Both arrows are levelwise quasi-isomorphisms: the first changes only cohomology above $b$, and the second only below $a$, all of which vanish. Here good truncation uses $\ker d^b$ at the upper endpoint and the quotient by $\operatorname{im}d^{a-1}$ at the lower endpoint (cohomology if $a=b$). These are simultaneous tower constructions because kernels and quotients are functorial. Finite pullback is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], so it preserves these truncations and quasi-isomorphisms. Thus finite comparisons on the bounded $B_n$ also specify them on $P_n$ through this zigzag. No boundedness of the terms of $P$ or finite Tor-amplitude of $M_n$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 099N (lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case), (5); simultaneous bounded representatives for its reduction formula

proof.text: For an $A_n$-complex $H$ on $s$, identify its identity geometric stalk with $\Gamma(s,H)$: every pointed neighbourhood $(U,u)$ receives the unique pointed map $u:(s,\mathrm{id})\to(U,u)$, and $[U,u,a]\mapsto u^*a$ is inverse to $a\mapsto[s,\mathrm{id},a]$ in the colimit of [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. Apply [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence] to $v$ and the identity point to obtain $e_{v,n}:\Gamma(s,v^*P_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}(P_n)_v$. These commute with quotient transitions: a reduction sends the representative section $a$ to its image $\bar a$, and both orders give $[U,u,\bar a]$. Exact point sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] commute with the cone model of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]: sheaf products have sectionwise products, so evaluation carries $(x_n)\mapsto(x_n-t_nx_{n+1})$ to the identical formula on sections and carries its cone and shift to their module versions. Consequently $J_v(M)$ is canonically the realization of the strict module tower $(P_n)_v$, through these $e_{v,n}$. This is an identification of whole cone complexes. The strict derived-limit functor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] transports the tower quasi-isomorphisms of Step 1, so the bounded replacement does not change this identification.

source.place: Tags 05V1 (lemma-point-morphism-sites), 0F4F (lemma-point-functor); proetale.tex Tag 0993 (lemma-classical-point); exact sections applied to the quotient cone

proof.text: Let $\chi_{v,f}:L(fv)^*\to Lv^*Lf^*$ be the specified integral compositor of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Define $c_{f,v,M}=\Gamma(s,\chi_{v,f,M}^{-1})$. The defining map $\eta_{v,f,M}$ of that node identifies $Lv^*Lf^*M$ with realization of the simultaneous tower $v^*f^*P_n$, and identifies this $c$ with the inverse of the finite composition map. More explicitly, in the finite stalk coordinates of Step 2 its map is $e_{fv,n}^{-1}\,c^{\mathrm{fin}}_{f,v,P_n}\,e_{v,f^*P_n}$. Indeed [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence] applied to $v,f$ and the identity point gives $e_{fv,n}=c^{\mathrm{fin}}_{f,v,P_n}\,e_{v,f^*P_n}\,\Gamma(s,\chi_{v,f,P_n})$. All coefficient transitions commute with this equation by their representative formulas. The integral realization node explicitly uses the counit of the entire reduction tower for $\eta$, and gives independence and naturality of these identifications. Thus this is exactly the required specified comparison, represented on the simultaneous diagrams. All iterated pullbacks remain in $D^b_c$ by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] (1), so every use of these integral identifications has its required domain.

source.place: Tag 099N (lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case), (2),(5); specified counit realization of pullback composition

proof.text: For $\delta=\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)$ define the tower map $R_{v,\alpha,n}:(P_n)_v\to(P_n)_{v\delta}$ by $[U,u,a]\mapsto[U,u\delta,a]$. The finite comparison node [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence] supplies this natural $A_n$-linear isomorphism on bounded complexes. It is also a strict tower map: reducing the section before or after this operation gives $[U,u\delta,\bar a]$. Its inverse is the same construction with $\delta^{-1}$, and therefore is a strict inverse. Transport its realization through the Step 2 identifications to define $r_{v,\alpha,M}$. Concretely a map $R_\bullet$ of towers gives the cone map $(b,a)\mapsto((\prod R_n)b,(\prod R_n)a)$; commuting with transitions makes this a chain map. Thus the construction specifies both coordinates of the cone, not just maps on reductions. Functoriality of strict derived limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] makes it an integral isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05V1 (lemma-point-morphism-sites), point functor reindexing; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok)

proof.text: The constructions are natural for every integral derived morphism, including ones not represented by a single map between the initially chosen resolutions. On chain maps the representative formulas for $e$, $c^{\mathrm{fin}}$ and $R$ are natural, and hence natural on the whole quotient diagram. The descent and resolution comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] identify the quotient-cone constructions from different K-flat representatives. Exact point sections preserve quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Thus these chain functors invert the arrows used to represent derived morphisms. The localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (2) descends their natural transformations uniquely, preserving identities and composition; naturality for the inverse of a quasi-isomorphism follows by multiplying its naturality square by its inverses. This proves resolution independence of $r$ as well as naturality for roofs. For $c$ it agrees with the already natural, resolution-independent $\eta$-construction of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization].

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); descent from chain maps through derived localization

proof.text: For $w:s\to Z$ use the same $P_\bullet$ on $X$ for every factor. On each finite level [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence] gives $c^{\mathrm{fin}}_{fh,w}=c^{\mathrm{fin}}_{f,hw}\,c^{\mathrm{fin}}_{h,w}\,(\chi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{h,f})_w$. The quotient formulas make this an equation of tower maps, as in Step 3. The associativity clause and the entire-tower counit normalization in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] identify all occurrences of the nested pullbacks with these simultaneous diagrams, including $J_w(\chi_{h,f,M})$. Applying the strict derived-limit functor and exact sections therefore gives precisely $c_{fh,w,M}=c_{f,hw,M}\circ c_{h,w,Lf^*M}\circ J_w(\chi_{h,f,M})$. At the identity morphism the finite comparison is the identity; the unit clause of the integral realization node gives $c_{\mathrm{id},v,M}=1$ under its specified identity identification. This also supplies $J_{\mathrm{id}}(N)=\operatorname{Fib}_sN$.

source.place: Tags 05V1 and 0F4F; composition and identity on the specified quotient diagrams

proof.text: The finite mixed equation is the one in [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence]. Its representative calculation is explicit: the pullback germ given by $(U,u',V,\theta,a)$ first maps to $[V,\operatorname{pr}_V\theta u',a]$; reparametrization then gives $[V,\operatorname{pr}_V\theta u'\delta,a]$. Reparametrizing $u'$ first and then applying the comparison gives exactly the same representative. Quotient reduction changes only $a$, so the equation holds on the entire strict tower. Under the identifications of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], these are the maps of Steps 3--4. Functoriality of strict realization therefore gives $r_{fv,\alpha,M}\circ c_{f,v,M}=c_{f,v\delta,M}\circ r_{v,\alpha,Lf^*M}$, as equality of the specified integral maps.

source.place: Tag 0F4F (lemma-point-functor), representative calculation for composition with a source automorphism

proof.text: The action law is an equality on representatives in [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]: successive reparametrizations send $[U,u,a]$ to $[U,u\delta,a]$ and then $[U,u\delta\epsilon,a]$, while a single reparametrization by $\delta\epsilon$ gives that same representative. Also $\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\beta)=\operatorname{Spec}(\beta\circ\alpha)$, because affine spectrum reverses ring-map composition. Identity reparametrization fixes every representative. These are strict tower equations, and the product maps on both cone coordinates obey the same composition law. Hence $r_{v\delta,\beta,M}\circ r_{v,\alpha,M}=r_{v,\beta\circ\alpha,M}$ and $r_{v,1,M}=1$. Induction on the number of automorphisms proves the finite-succession assertion: appending one automorphism uses this two-factor identity, with the zero-length succession the identity.

source.place: Tag 05V1 (lemma-point-morphism-sites), functoriality under reindexing the pointed-neighbourhood colimit

proof.text: For a complex $N$ on $s$, let $\rho_{\delta,N}:\Gamma(s,N)\to\Gamma(s,\delta^{-1}N)$ be restriction along $\delta$, followed by inverse-image insertion. The site-equivalence formula of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] identifies the target with sections of $N$ over $(s\xrightarrow{\delta}s)$; restriction along the isomorphism $\delta$ has inverse restriction along $\delta^{-1}$, so $\rho$ is an isomorphism. The specified map of the question is $j_{\delta,N}=\Gamma(s,\kappa^\delta_N)\rho_{\delta,N}$. For integral constructible $N$, [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization] says this SPECIFIED $\kappa$ is natural and invertible and is the quotient-cone map with zero shifted coordinate. Its hypothesis holds since $N\in D^b_c(s,R)$ is derived complete. For a finite-coefficient sheaf, a section $a\in N(s)$ under restriction, insertion and $\kappa$ is the pullback-unit germ with source lift $\mathrm{id}_s$ and target lift $\delta$. The finite comparison formula sends it to $[s,\delta,a]$. This is also $r^{\mathrm{fin}}_{\mathrm{id},\alpha}([s,\mathrm{id},a])$. This proves the section equation at finite level directly from the normalizations.

source.place: Tags 05V1 and 0F4F; inverse-image insertion at the identity point; integral normalization by the specified quotient cone

proof.text:
Use one flat-term K-flat $Q\xrightarrow{q}N$ and $Q_n$ for all factors. Let $\mathcal H_v=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_n(Q_n)_v\to\prod_n(Q_n)_v)[-1]$, and let $e_v:J_v(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H_v$ be the whole-cone identification of Step 2. For $v=\mathrm{id}$ its source is $\Gamma(s,N)$ via Step 6. The normalization theorem [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization], with $g=\mathrm{id}$, identifies $e_{\mathrm{id}}$ with sections of the actual completion unit, followed by the identity-stalk identifications; this unit is invertible on the derived-complete domain. Thus $e_{\mathrm{id}}\Gamma(q)$ sends $z$ to $(0,([s,\mathrm{id},\bar z_n])_n)$. By [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], $j_{\delta,N}\Gamma(q)$ uses these same reductions, restricted along $\delta$, with zero shifted coordinate. Step 9 and the specified compositor realization [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] therefore give
$$e_\delta c_{\delta,\mathrm{id},N}j_{\delta,N}\Gamma(q)(z)=(0,([s,\delta,\bar z_n])_n)=\operatorname{Cone}(R_{\mathrm{id},\alpha,\bullet})e_{\mathrm{id}}\Gamma(q)(z).$$
These are equal chain maps on $\Gamma(s,Q)$, including the shifted coordinate. Exact sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] make $\Gamma(q)$ an isomorphism after localization. Cancel it and $e_\delta$; the definition of $r$ in Step 4 now gives $c_{\delta,\mathrm{id},N}j_{\delta,N}=r_{\mathrm{id},\alpha,N}$. This proves equality of the specified maps without using detection by reduction projections.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), comparison of the actual quotient-cone maps; proetale.tex Tag 099N (5)

proof.text: Apply Step 10 to $N=Lv^*M$, which is constructible by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] (1). The mixed equation of Step 7 and the compositor identity of Step 6 allow each occurrence of a source automorphism to pass through $c_{f,v}$ with exactly the displayed reparametrized point. For successive automorphisms, replace each $c_{\delta,\mathrm{id}}j_\delta$ by $r$ using Step 10, then combine adjacent $r$'s by Step 8. This proves compatibility with any finite succession and with the comparison for any $v$. All constructions are $R$-linear, since the finite maps preserve scalar multiplication and products, cones and sections carry the induced $R$-action. Finally use [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]: on objects rationalization uses the same integral representatives, and on morphisms $f\otimes a$ the fiber map is $a(\Gamma(s,f)\otimes E)$. Send the integral comparison families and their equalities through these functors. Naturality for arbitrary rational morphisms follows by this formula and linearity, first for a simple tensor and then for a finite sum. Inverses remain inverses. This gives all assertions for $E$, with no Weil datum or integrality assumption on the morphisms.
